sentence: The NHS says severe or long-lasting loneliness might increase the risk of some physical conditions, such as dementia.
It also says it might increase the risk of mental health conditions such as stress, anxiety, low mood or depression.
The NHS says loneliness is subjective and can be felt in a busy city or a rural area, online, or while with other people.
Significant life events, such as moving home or having a baby, can trigger it.
NHS suggestions include keeping in touch regularly with friends and family, including through short calls or messages.
Joining a group or club is described as a good way to connect and meet people.
Volunteering is also described as a good way to meet people.
Enjoyable activities such as time outdoors, exercise, reading or podcasts are said to improve wellbeing.
The NHS also suggests talking openly about how loneliness feels, and notes that comparing yourself with others, especially on social media, can make you feel lonelier.
For older people, the NHS suggests calling or video-chatting with family, joining local groups, starting small conversations when out, and planning things to look forward to.
The NHS suggests speaking to a GP about social prescribing, which connects people with a link worker who can point to local support.
For stress, anxiety or depression linked to loneliness, NHS talking therapies are available.
The NHS advises against using alcohol, cigarettes, gambling or drugs to cope with loneliness, because they can contribute to poor mental health.
If loneliness comes with low mood or anxiety that is lasting or affecting daily life, a GP appointment is the usual route.
Loneliness can make everything feel harder. If it has become overwhelming, people are there to talk at any hour.

sentence: For urgent help that is not an emergency, NHS 111 has a mental health option (option 2), which trusts describe as available at any time, for yourself or on someone else's behalf.

sentence: Samaritans listen at any time of day or night, and the number, 116 123, is free to call.
